#### 1. dominant beta-thalassemia  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.424)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6798695)

Mutations in CANT1 lead to skeletal dysplasia by disrupting bone development pathways. Mutations in HBB lead to anemia by disrupting hemoglobin synthesis and erythropoiesis. Reduced erythropoiesis and hemoglobin synthesis can secondarily impair bone development, creating a convergence point.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of specific genetic variants in HBB that cause a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect in beta-thalassemia, or variants in CANT1 that cause a gain-of-function effect in Desbuquois dysplasia 1, would falsify the proposed loss-of-function mechanism for both diseases and thus the shared module hypothesis. _(variant: rs33997230 (a common variant in HBB associated with beta-thalassemia trait) with an allele frequency > 1% in relevant populations.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding this overlap could inform therapeutic strategies, such as targeting bone health in beta-thalassemia patients or investigating hematopoietic stem cell contributions to skeletal integrity in Desbuquois dysplasia 1.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular pathways, even if indirectly, between skeletal dysplasias and anemias could reveal novel therapeutic targets for managing growth deficits in hematologic disorders or for improving bone health in anemic patients.
